On Fri, 28 May 2027 at 08:22 -07:00, Tessa Morgan wrote:
> Quick hypothesis: a cold set of prefix keys for BrightCart may be causing KV cache warmup combined with large, unbounded client batching that effectively stalls hot lanes (head-of-line blocking).

Confirmed — initial telemetry snapshot (attaching) shows BrightCart's prefix hit rate dropped from 96% to 12% starting at 07:48. Simultaneously we see a jump in request batch sizes from their SDK: median batch size = 1.2 -> 16.7 and a tail of batches > 64. Several inference workers show queue depth saturating and upstream gateway returning 502s.

Short plan:
1) Immediate mitigation (10–20m): throttle client-side max_batched_tokens for BrightCart via per-tenant policy to cap batch size at 8 and enable early response fallback to smaller model variant.
2) Medium (30–90m): apply targeted KV pre-warm for BrightCart's active prefixes, enable prefix-adaptive heater to reduce cold-miss penalty.
3) Postmortem/optimize: tune batching window heuristics and add an SLA-exempt fast-path for small-latency non-batched calls.

Requesting Marissa to coordinate an exec sync if we need credits/SLA exceptions for the fallbacks. Ben — can you stage the per-tenant policy now (non-disruptive)?

—Vivek

Triage update and ask for exec awareness:

What happened: a combination of BrightCart's SDK update this morning (released 07:30) reduced the batching time threshold and inadvertently caused many small requests to be aggregated into oversized batches under a specific pattern. Those oversized batches hit a cold set of KV keys (experimental product prefactors) meaning cache warmup was sequential and blocked hot lanes. The runtime's continuous batching logic then created backpressure that cascaded to edge gateways.

Impact: increased p99 latency from ~120ms -> 1.8s for price-preview route; error rate on that route jumped to 18% for the 20-minute window. Estimated customer transactions impacted: ~2.1k.

Immediate actions taken:
- Per-tenant policy applied: max_batch_size=8, enable fallbacks to smaller variant (non-SLA impacting path).
- Applied targeted KV pre-warm for the top 200 prefixes for BrightCart (expected warm hit recovery in ~6–8 minutes).
- Opened a hotfix with SDK team and asked BrightCart to roll back the SDK change if they can.

Requested: executive visibility for potential credit & SLA make-good; Diane, can you confirm whether this window caused revenue-impacting checkout failures? Tessa — I'll prepare a short executive blurb for your sponsor.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com, diane.meyer@brightcart.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [PROD] sudden error spike + 500s during morning surge

Done and confirmed: per-tenant policy staged and rolled to 5% canary for BrightCart at 09:08, then 100% at 09:11. Observed p99 latency dropping to ~250ms by 09:16 as KV hits recovered and batch sizes normalized.

Notes for post-incident: we should add a protection to avoid allowing the client-side SDK to multiply batch windows with server-side batching heuristics (double-batching). Also add a soft quota on in-flight batch token count per tenant to prevent queue starvation.

—Ben
Ben Carter
